### SSO Events by Application

The total number of SSO events recorded for each application over a selected time
period.

IBM Verify raises an SSO event when someone who is already signed in reaches an
application. It uses the CanadaLogin session they already hold, so the person
enters no password and no second factor. This metric is useful for understanding usage
volume across CanadaLogin-integrated applications. It counts events, not people:
one person reaching an application several times contributes several events.

The source column is `total_logins`, but the event it counts is what IBM Verify
calls an SSO event, part of application usage.

*Alternative names*:

- application usage
- SSO event volume
- single sign-on events
- total uses of CanadaLogin by application

**Calculation.** Sum `total_logins` over the selected reporting period, grouped
by application.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Example Queries"}

::: {.panel-tabset}

## SQL

```sql
SELECT
  application_name,
  SUM(total_logins) AS total_sso_events
FROM   ibm_verify.app_login_counts
-- set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
WHERE  from_date BETWEEN DATE '2026-01-01' AND DATE '2026-05-28'
-- optionally filter out internal applications; see the internal applications
-- note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  AND application_name NOT IN (
      SELECT al.alias
      FROM   rp.alias al
      JOIN   rp.service s ON al.rp_id = s.rp_id
      WHERE  s.is_internal
  )
GROUP  BY application_name
ORDER  BY total_sso_events DESC;
```

## R

```r
internal_apps <- tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "alias")) |>
  inner_join(tbl(con, in_schema("rp", "service")), by = "rp_id") |>
  filter(is_internal) |>
  select(application_name = alias)

tbl(con, in_schema("ibm_verify", "app_login_counts")) |>
  # set the reporting window; see the timespans note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  filter(
    from_date >= as.Date("2026-01-01"),
    from_date <= as.Date("2026-05-28")
  ) |>
  # optionally filter out internal applications; see the internal applications
  # note in cookbook/notes.qmd
  anti_join(internal_apps, by = "application_name") |>
  group_by(application_name) |>
  summarise(
    total_sso_events = sum(total_logins, na.rm = TRUE)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(total_sso_events))
```

:::

:::

*Interpretation notes.* This counts events, not people. Use this metric when the
question is about system usage or activity volume. Use unique user metrics when
the question is about reach.

These are a different IBM Verify event type from the CanadaLogin-wide
[authentication events](#authentication-events), so never add the two together or
present them side by side as comparable figures. Unlike the authentication
events, SSO events are not inflated by second factors, because reaching an
application uses the session the person already holds rather than asking them
to authenticate again.
